subject: Post-demo: payment route, deployment fit, and procurement readiness
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Nora Patel <nora@fintechpros.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: payment route, deployment fit, and procurement readiness

Hi Nora — thanks again for your time on the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so procurement has what they need: 

1) Commercial path options we discussed
   - Hosted (on-demand): immediate onboarding, pay-by-card or invoice. Good for proof-of-value with minimal lead time.
   - Dedicated (reserved capacity/commits): preferred for sustained throughput; can be contract + monthly commit (SLA). Procurement typically requires PO+contract.
   - Private (VPC/on-prem): for regulated workloads — enterprise licensing + implementation timeline; usually involves SSO/KMS integration.

2) Payment flows we should confirm
   - Procurement preference: PO vs corporate card? (You mentioned procurement tends to require POs for platform spends.)
   - Marketplace interest: do you want to route this through your cloud marketplace (AWS Marketplace) to simplify procurement? That can change the billing and invoicing path.

3) Pricing/packaging notes for your team
   - For a pilot, recommend Hosted on-demand to reduce procurement friction.
   - If you need predictable unit economics at scale, Dedicated (commits) saves ~25–35% depending on GPU mix — we can put ranges in a matrix.

4) Next steps (proposed)
   - You: confirm whether Procurement will accept a card for pilot or needs PO (and approximate PO lead time).
   - We: share a short SOW draft + pricing matrix and a marketplace option summary.
   - If Procurement needs contract/PO, loop in Stephanie (legal/sales ops) to expedite standard terms.

I attached a one-page pricing matrix and a draft SOW for your internal review. If it helps, Marissa can coordinate a short call with Procurement to walk the path options and show the ASP (approx. spend profile) for each.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min call with procurement if that accelerates things.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attach: SOW_redwood_draft_v1.pdf (application/pdf), pricing-matrix_FTP.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Nora Patel <nora@fintechpros.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir@fintechpros.com>, Procurement <procurement@fintechpros.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: payment route, deployment fit, and procurement readiness

Karthik — great recap, thanks. A few notes from Procurement and infra: 

- Procurement: For pilots under $25k we usually allow corporate card. Anything expected over that goes through PO and takes ~2–3 weeks for processing (internal approvals + AP). We'll confirm a hard threshold tomorrow.
- Marketplace: We prefer AWS Marketplace for SaaS where possible (helps our internal chargeback). If Redwood supports Marketplace listing and equivalent commercial terms, Procurement will favor that.
- Deployment fit: Security flagged that VPC/private will need an architecture review and KMS discussion — that's a 4–6 week timeline.

Can you send the SOW with two alternate pricing lines: (A) Hosted pilot on-demand by card and (B) Dedicated 12-month commit with PO? Also please include the SKU-level commit and the expected monthly spend range so I can flag to Finance.

If you can, include a short note about whether Dedicated commits can be started as a short-term (90-day) pilot and converted to full-year commits — Procurement asked if there’s flexibility on commit ramp.

Thanks,
Nora
Director of Product Operations | FinTech Pros

On Mon, Jun 30, 2025 at 3:04 PM Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com> wrote:
> (original message above)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: payment route, deployment fit, and procurement readiness

Karthik — forwarding Nora's note. Quick internal alignment: 

- If Procurement wants AWS Marketplace, we have a listing but need to confirm the pricing parity and Marketplace fees (that can slightly increase unit cost). I can pull the Marketplace addendum language.
- On commit flexibility: we typically require a 12-month commitment for the full discount band, but we can offer a 90-day trial addendum that converts to the remainder upon signature (sales-approved). We should decide what to propose as an explicit conversion clause to reduce procurement back-and-forth.
- I'll volunteer to join a procurement call; I can own the marketplace/contract language. Steph — can you prepare the standard short-form PO-friendly terms and the conversion clause?

Suggested response items to Nora: 
  1) Two SOW lines (Hosted pilot by card, Dedicated 12mo PO with SKU-level commit and monthly spend bands).
  2) Explicit note on commit-to-convert (90-day trial -> remaining term) and marketplace parity caveat.
  3) Offer Marissa+Stephanie to join procurement call.

—Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

On Tue, Jul 1, 2025 at 9:22 AM Nora Patel <nora@fintechpros.com> wrote:
> (Nora's message above)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Nora Patel <nora@fintechpros.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jul 2025 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: payment route, deployment fit, and procurement readiness

Nora — thanks for the clarity. A few items from our side: 

- Attached is a one-page extract of our standard short-form terms for PO-led purchases and a simple conversion addendum for a 90-day pilot (if the customer signs within that period, the pilot fees convert and the remainder of the 12-month commit invoices per the agreed schedule).
- Marketplace: we can support AWS Marketplace billing; there is a small marketplace fee that impacts net price to Redwood but we can show a marketplace-equivalent line in the pricing matrix. If you prefer Marketplace we’ll include an “AWS Marketplace” line and a note about equivalent service levels.
- SKU-level commits: we will provide three commit bands (Small / Medium / Large) with expected monthly token throughput and approximate monthly spend. That will let Finance map to chargeback codes.

Next steps: 
  1) Karthik/Marissa: share the revised SOW with both Hosted and Dedicated lines + pricing matrix (include marketplace equivalent).
  2) Nora: confirm whether Procurement will allow corporate card for the pilot or require PO. If PO, please indicate expected PO lead time.
  3) If Procurement prefers, happy to schedule 20–30 min call later this week to review.

Thanks — attaching terms now.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
attach: RDW_shortform_PO_terms_excerpt.pdf (application/pdf)
